question_text: Terry measures the dimensions of a box as $15\text{ cm}$ by $12\text{ cm}$ by $8\text{ cm}$, rounded to the nearest centimetre.

subparts.stem: Use Terry's measurements to estimate the volume of the box.

mark_breakdown.desc: Estimating dimensions to the nearest cm and multiplying

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Estimated volume of a cuboid is found by multiplying estimated dimensions.
step_by_step: Round each dimension to the nearest integer: $15.3 \to 15$, $11.8 \to 12$, $8.4 \to 8$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Rounding the exact calculated volume instead of rounding the dimensions before calculating.

subparts.stem: The actual dimensions of the box are $15.3\text{ cm}$ by $11.8\text{ cm}$ by $8.4\text{ cm}$. Find the actual volume of the box.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Volume of a rectangular prism is $V = l \times w \times h$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Rounding the result when the question asks for the exact/actual volume.

subparts.stem: Find the absolute and percentage error in Terry's estimate.

mark_breakdown.desc: Applying the absolute error formula $|V_A - V_E|$
Applying the percentage error formula $\frac{|V_A - V_E|}{V_E} \times 100\%$

subparts.solution:
$\text{Absolute error} = |V_A - V_E| = |1440 - 1516.536|\text{ cm}^3 = |-76.536|\text{ cm}^3 \approx 76.536\text{ cm}^3$
$\text{Percentage error} = \frac{|V_A - V_E|}{V_E} \times 100\% = \frac{76.536}{1516.536} \times 100\% \approx 5.05\%$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Absolute error is $|V_A - V_E|$ where $V_A$ is the approximated value and $V_E$ is the exact value. Percentage error is $\frac{|V_A - V_E|}{V_E} \times 100\%$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Dividing by the approximated value $V_A$ instead of the exact value $V_E$.
